channel.title: Rich Robertson Blog
channel.description: Thoughts, lessons learned, and deep dives from Rich Robertson on software engineering, cloud platforms, and distributed systems.

item.title: How I Built the AskRich Chatbot for Technical Screening
item.description: A practical breakdown of how AskRich works: recruiter-focused prompts, citation-backed answers, API integration, and deployment decisions.

item.title: What It Took to Modernize a Legacy Service Across 32 Global Regions
item.description: A practical engineering breakdown of modernizing a legacy backend service across 32 global regions with reliability, rollout safety, and operational continuity.

item.title: What Is Eventual Consistency? (Explained Simply)
item.description: A simple explanation of eventual consistency: what it means, why distributed systems use it, and how it differs from strong consistency.

item.title: What Is the CAP Theorem? (Explained Simply)
item.description: A simple explanation of the CAP theorem: consistency, availability, partition tolerance, and how distributed systems navigate the trade-offs between them.

item.title: What Is Idempotency? (And Why It Matters in Distributed Systems)
item.description: A simple explanation of idempotency: what it means, why retries require it, and how to design idempotent APIs and distributed operations.

item.title: API Backpressure Explained Simply
item.description: A simple guide to API backpressure: what it is, why rate limiting is not enough, and how systems stay stable under load.

item.title: Designing a Correct Distributed Lease Service: Tenure on Raft
item.description: A distributed systems deep dive on building a correct lease service with Raft, leader-based time authority, fencing tokens, and failure handling.

item.title: Distributed Systems Interview Guide
item.description: A practical distributed systems interview guide covering the concepts, trade-offs, and examples worth studying before senior backend and platform engineering interviews.

item.title: Raft vs Paxos vs EPaxos: A Practical Guide
item.description: A practical comparison of Raft, Paxos, and EPaxos: where each fits, trade-offs in complexity and latency, and how to choose for production systems.

item.title: What Is a Control Plane?
item.description: A simple explanation of what a control plane is, how it differs from a data plane, and why cloud platforms rely on control-plane systems.

item.title: What Is a Distributed Lock? (With Examples)
item.description: A practical guide to distributed locks with real examples: lock ownership, lease time, fencing tokens, and common failure modes in production systems.

item.title: Polyglot Architectures: A Case for Functional Languages in Distributed Systems
item.description: A distributed systems architecture analysis of where functional languages fit alongside object-oriented platforms in backend and cloud systems.

item.title: Programming Language Selection in Distributed Systems: A Strategic, Long-Term Perspective
item.description: A comparative analysis of Go, Rust, Java, and Python for distributed systems through the lens of concurrency, memory safety, tail-latency behavior, workload fit, and architectural cost placement.

item.title: Designing Backpressure in GraphQL Using CDN Latency Signals
item.description: Using CDN latency signals to implement adaptive backpressure in GraphQL systems and maintain stability under adversarial load.

item.title: Latency-Aware Backpressure with Server-Timing in CDN-Fronted Distributed Systems
item.description: An analysis of how Server-Timing and CDN edge timing can improve backpressure decisions through latency attribution, even when full distributed tracing is unavailable.

item.title: Backpressure in Distributed Systems: Stability, Correctness, and Graceful Degradation
item.description: A distributed systems deep dive on backpressure, admission control, bounded queues, adaptive concurrency, and graceful degradation in backend services.

item.title: Why a Three-Node Kafka Cluster Is Often Preferable to a Five-Node Cluster
item.description: A distributed-systems analysis of why three-node Kafka clusters are often preferable to five-node deployments under common replication and acknowledgment configurations.

item.title: Architecting a Multitenant Control Plane for a Next-Generation Data Tier
item.description: A cloud architecture deep dive on multitenant control planes, durable command queues, workflow orchestration, distributed workers, and tenant isolation.

item.title: Kafka at Hyperscale
item.description: An analysis of why partition-centric streaming systems encounter coordination, rebalancing, storage-compute coupling, and workflow-orchestration limits at hyperscale.
